title: The silent hook
ticket: I added a PreToolUse hook in .devin/hooks.v1.json to block rm -rf but it never fires.

commands.output:
pass  custom subagent profiles   none configured
pass  otel exporter environment  no unsupported OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables set

2 check(s): 2 passed, 0 warning(s), 0 failure(s)

total 12
drwxr-xr-x 2 customer customer 4096 Sep 30 03:00 .
drwxr-xr-x 4 customer customer 4096 Sep 30 03:00 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 customer customer  184 Sep 30 03:00 hooks.v1.json

No rules found.

To create rules, add files to one of these directories:
Devin rules:
  .windsurf/rules/*.md (always-on)

Cursor rules:
  .cursor/rules/*.md (conditional)

  Current directory: /home/customer/project

root_cause.q: What is wrong with the hook file?
choices: The standalone .devin/hooks.v1.json file must be the hooks object itself, without a top-level hooks wrapper.
Hooks need organization enablement before PreToolUse can fire.
The event name must be pre_tool_use.
Project hooks only load from ~/.config/devin.
Remove the wrapper so PreToolUse is top-level, or move the hooks object under hooks in .devin/config.json; verify with /hooks.
Add --sandbox and leave the file unchanged.
Restart with --permission-mode dangerous.
Rename the file to hooks.json.

explain: The standalone file's top-level object is the hooks mapping; settings and config files nest it under hooks.

title: The missing Node binary
ticket: Devin keeps saying `node: command not found`, but node works in my terminal.

root_cause.q: Why does Devin not find node?
choices: Node is only an alias; aliases and functions are not exported as environment variables, and Devin snapshots the login-shell environment at startup.
The Devin sandbox blocks node by default.
Devin does not support nvm-managed Node.
The PATH variable is too long.
Export the nvm bin directory in the shell profile and restart Devin, which snapshots the environment once at startup.
Run /clear.
Run devin update.
Start Devin with --sandbox.

explain: The alias can work in a terminal but is not an exported environment variable. Devin takes a login-shell environment snapshot at startup.

title: Print mode in CI
ticket: `devin -p` works on my laptop but fails in our CI job in a freshly cloned repo.

commands.output:
Error: Refusing to run in an untrusted workspace: /home/customer/app

--respect-workspace-trust [<RESPECT_WORKSPACE_TRUST>]
          Respect workspace trust settings

root_cause.q: Why can print mode fail in the fresh CI clone?
choices: Print mode cannot display the workspace-trust prompt and fails in an untrusted directory.
Print mode cannot run when DEVIN_MODEL is set.
The directory must be started with --sandbox.
The -c flag is required for print mode.
Pass --respect-workspace-trust false (or set respect_workspace_trust: false in config), or trust the directory by starting devin interactively there once.
Set DEVIN_MODEL.
Use --sandbox.
Use -c.

explain: Print mode cannot show the workspace-trust prompt, so in a fresh clone it refuses to run (recorded from devin 3000.11.3). CI should pass --respect-workspace-trust false.

title: The stubborn git push prompt
ticket: I run with --permission-mode dangerous but Devin still asks before every git push. Bug?

commands.output: cat: .devin/config.local.json: No such file or directory

pass  custom subagent profiles   none configured
pass  otel exporter environment  no unsupported OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables set

2 check(s): 2 passed, 0 warning(s), 0 failure(s)

root_cause.q: Why does dangerous mode still prompt for git push?
choices: An organization/team ask rule applies; org deny and ask rules cannot be overridden by permission modes or local config.
Dangerous mode is deprecated.
Project config overrides all CLI flags.
Smart mode's model judged git push unsafe.
A team admin must change Team Settings; the user cannot override it locally.
Add an allow entry in config.local.json.
Use /bypass.
Delete the cache file.

explain: Team settings outrank local permission modes; the guide says organization deny/ask rules remain active even in dangerous or bypass mode.

title: The old binary on PATH
ticket: I ran `devin update` twice and it says I'm on the latest, but `devin --version` still shows an old version.

root_cause.q: Why does devin --version still show the old version?
choices: An older second copy earlier on PATH shadows the updated ~/.local/bin/devin.
The update command needs --force.
The CLI cache is stale.
The installer must be run with sudo.
Remove the stale copy or fix PATH order, run hash -r, and verify with type -a devin.
Run devin update --force.
Clear ~/.cache/devin.
Reinstall with sudo.

explain: The shell uses the first matching executable on PATH; an older /usr/local/bin copy shadows the updated user install.

title: The hook from another tool
ticket: Some hook keeps blocking my commands with 'blocked by policy' but I have no Devin hooks configured.

commands.output: ls: cannot access '.devin': No such file or directory

total 12
drwxr-xr-x 2 customer customer 4096 Sep 30 03:00 .
drwxr-xr-x 4 customer customer 4096 Sep 30 03:00 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 customer customer  256 Sep 30 03:00 settings.json

root_cause.q: Where does the blocking hook come from?
choices: Devin imports hooks from .claude/settings.json because read_config_from.claude is on by default.
An organization policy always imports hooks.
The OS sandbox is blocking the command.
The sessions.db file is corrupted.

fix.q: How can the customer stop importing that hook?
choices: Remove the hook or set read_config_from.claude=false in user config; confirm its source with /hooks.
Delete sessions.db.
Disable the sandbox.
Add a Windsurf rule.

explain: The CLI imports Claude Code config by default; the hook's settings file reveals the source.

title: The filesystem server that never starts

commands.output:
Configured MCP servers:

  • fs
    Command: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystm /home/customer/docs

root_cause.q: Why do the filesystem tools not appear?
choices: The stdio server package name is misspelled, so the server never starts.
The organization disallows MCP.
The server requires devin mcp login.
Filesystem servers require HTTP transport.
Remove fs, then add it again with @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem; verify the command manually first.
Run devin mcp enable fs.
Restart the terminal.
Add mcp__fs__* to the allow list.

explain: The recorded CLI output shows the misspelled package in the local project MCP configuration.
